script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

JESSICA (30s), a hardworking nurse, is sitting on the couch. She's lost in thought, holding a photo of her deceased husband. The phone rings, bringing her back to reality.

JESSICA
(answering)
Hello?

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(on the phone)
Hi, it's me.

Jessica looks surprised as she recognizes the voice.

JESSICA
(surprised)
Maggie?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Maggie (30s), a former classmate of Jessica, sits across from her, a steaming cup of coffee in front of her.

MAGGIE
(smiling)
It's been a long time. I've been thinking about you.

Jessica looks skeptical but invites Maggie to sit down.

JESSICA
(curious)
Why now?

MAGGIE
(pausing)
I found your address in my old yearbook. I wanted to apologize.

INT. JESSICA'S KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jessica is cooking dinner while her son, MIKEY (8), helps.

MIKEY
(innocently)
Mom, who was that lady?

Jessica hesitates, looking worried.

JESSICA
(nervously)
Just an old friend, Mikey.

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

Flashback to 20 years ago. Jessica and Maggie are in high school, sitting at their desks. Maggie is teasing Jessica about her husband, who was absent due to military deployment.

MAGGIE
(teasing)
Your husband isn't even here, and you're already mourning him.

Jessica looks hurt and upset.

JESSICA
(defensively)
He's my husband, Maggie. I love him.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Back in the present.

MAGGIE
(apologetic)
I was just being cruel. I'm so sorry, Jessica. I didn't mean it.

Jessica looks at Maggie, considering her words.

JESSICA
(softly)
It's okay, Maggie. But why now? What's changed?

MAGGIE
(sadly)
I've had a wake-up call. I've lost someone close to me, and I realize how important it is to make amends.

INT. JESSICA'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jessica is sitting on the couch, holding the photo of her husband once again. She looks up as she hears a knock on the door.

JESSICA
(surprised)
Maggie?

INT. ENTRANCEWAY - NIGHT

Maggie stands nervously at the door, holding a bouquet of flowers.

MAGGIE
(apologetic)
I know this might be a surprise, but I really want to make things right between us.

Jessica hesitates, then opens the door, allowing Maggie in. They sit down together, and Jessica accepts the flowers.

JESSICA
(softly)
I forgive you, Maggie.

INT. PARK - DAY

Jessica and Maggie are sitting on a park bench, surrounded by cherry blossoms. They talk about their past, their present, and their hopes for the future.

JESSICA
(reflecting)
I never thought I'd be able to forgive you. But I'm glad I did.

MAGGIE
(tearfully)
Me too. I never wanted to hurt you. I'm so sorry.

They share a moment of understanding and mutual forgiveness.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
